summary: The study investigates the effect of NH3 plasma pretreatment on the ALD of Al2O3 on GaAs substrates. The process uses trimethylaluminum and water vapor as precursors at 300 °C. The NH3 plasma pretreatment improves the electrical properties and reduces surface defects by decreasing GaAs oxides and elemental As.
evidence: Al2O3 thin films were deposited by atomic layer deposition on HF-cleaned and NH3 plasma-treated GaAs surfaces, respectively. The precursors used for Al2O3 films are trimethylaluminum and water. The deposition temperature was fixed at 300 °C. NH3 plasma pretreatment efficiently decreases the formation of GaAs oxides and suppresses the interfacial layer regrowth, and thus leads to a larger accumulation capacitance.
